prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and its experimental discovery in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep topological insulators as my preferred configuration, but I have tested it against the chair's questions and I hold it more narrowly than in round 1. The chain is what persuades me: Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling in graphene-like bands gives a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states, and Molenkamp's group then found the quantised edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, a prediction that nature could have refused and did not. That is a discovery in the sense I care about, a clue from nature confirmed by independent groups for almost two decades, and it reorganised how we classify electronic matter and fed materials and device work. The citation I would defend is deliberately limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification, which keeps a clear theory-to-experiment line and does not claim the whole later field. No member calls the science premature, and several call it overdue, which separates it from B015 on maturity.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is the real weakness and round 1 did not remove it. Eriksson and Olsson would replace Mele with Hasan, I would replace nobody, and in either version Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who proposed HgTe, and Fu, who generalised to 3D, stay outside the trio. A prize that names Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is defensible as a statement about the quantum spin Hall effect, but it will be read as ignoring the 3D materials branch that most people mean by topological insulators. The overlap with the topological phase transitions honoured in 2016 is a further discount. Only five members ranked B053, no one but me ranks it first, and I should not treat the fact that colleagues call it mature as a vote for my particular trio. If the committee finds that the attribution cannot be defended, B057 is the cleaner configuration and I would not obstruct it.

responses.point: Lindroth defends lattice clocks as a secure, reproduced result with a pair of laureates that all eight opening ballots share, and answers my worry that it is engineering by calling the magic-wavelength idea a physics step distinct from the comb and ion control.
responses.response: I accept her correction in part. The magic-wavelength condition, where the differential light shift cancels, is a physical idea and not a technical polish, and the comb is the ruler while ion control is another architecture, so I no longer call lattice clocks incremental engineering. That is why I have moved B057 from my sixth place to the head of my alternatives. What stops me from leading with it is not rigour but the question of what the committee learns about nature: clocks at 1e-18 are a superb measurement, yet the 2005 and 2012 prizes already honoured this line, and the unfinished redefinition of the second makes the consequence still ahead of us. I would vote for it without reluctance if the committee prefers a clean attribution to a conceptual shift.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks magic-angle graphene first but writes that if the committee wants maturity over cleanliness of attribution he would move to B053, and that a B053 prize would have to decide between Mele and Hasan.
responses.response: That conditional is useful, because it suggests that the gap between B015 and B053 is narrow for him and for me. We agree on the names Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and we agree that the 2016 overlap is a discount and not a bar. Where I still differ is on his claim that the moire trio is tighter: the prediction and the decisive experiment do come from the credited people, but Yuan Cao and the Dean group are outside, and Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto preceded Bistritzer and MacDonald. His line that maturity should decide between two conceptual candidates is the rule I would apply, and under it B053 is ahead of B015 by roughly ten years of reproduction.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers magic-angle graphene on the grounds that the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero experiment close a falsifiable loop and that eight years of confirmation answers the maturity objection, and he thinks the Mele-versus-Hasan choice and the 2016 overlap favour B015.
responses.response: The falsifiable loop is a real strength and I do not dismiss it. But Kane-Mele and the HgTe experiment is also a loop closed by a prediction, and an older one. I also do not accept that the 2016 overlap tips the balance, because topological insulators concern band topology protected by time reversal in a clean insulator, while moire graphene is about strong correlation in flat bands, and I would not call one a continuation of the other, though I admit the committee will hear the objection. On his claim that the Hasan work is the most convincing part, I agree that ARPES surface-state maps are decisive for 3D, but a prize can only mean one thing at a time, and I would rather give a precise 2D citation than a diluted one that leaves out Mele and still omits Fu and the others.

responses.point: Olsson argues that a prize requires an original verified observation and not a settled mechanism, that the correlated phases in magic-angle graphene are widely reproduced, and that a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio is theory-heavy and leaves the 3D discovery unrecognised.
responses.response: I now agree with her on the mechanism: a citation that says correlated insulating and superconducting states were discovered, without naming the pairing mechanism, would be honest, and my objection from round 1 that the physics is unresolved is weaker than my objection that it is young. I am less moved by theory-heavy, since Molenkamp's group provided the observation that gives the 2D chain its experimental half, and Kane and Mele provided the idea; the sequence matches the one she values in B015. Her point that the 3D discovery is left out is correct and it is the cost of the configuration. I would accept that cost in exchange for not splitting Kane and Mele, but I recognise that this is a judgment and not a proof.

responses.point: Pearce moved from IceCube to optical lattice clocks, saying a Nobel Prize rewards the demonstrated measurement advance and not its later standardisation, and that the committee is choosing between breadth of agreement and perceived novelty.
responses.response: I agree with his framing of the choice and with the argument that the redefinition of the second is a consequence of the discovery and not a condition for it, which answers one of the chair's questions. I disagree only on how to settle it: breadth of agreement is a fact about our rankings, and rankings reflect where each of us is expert, so I give it limited weight as evidence. I also accept his point about IceCube. No member now puts B054 first and the credit among Halzen, Karle and Spiering is not unique, so I have dropped it from my alternatives and I am not pressing it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can defend Kane, Mele and Molenkamp without Hasan, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Fu, or whether the omission of the 3D branch will be seen as a misstatement of the field.
Whether topological insulators are distinct enough from the topological phase transitions honoured in 2016.
Whether lattice clocks should be viewed as a third achievement in optical metrology and whether the pending redefinition of the second is a reason to wait.
Whether a two-part configuration is workable at all: with at most three people in total, any pairing leaves at most one name for the second part, which I think would distort both.
I rely on my own recollection of the credit history; the committee files do not verify individual roles, and I defer to colleagues in atomic and condensed-matter physics on the experimental details.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. David Gross and Thomas Van Riet are not connected to these achievements, and I have no known connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan, Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer. I note the disclosures by Johansson and Kroll concerning B021 and Kroll's Boulder link on B057, and I see nothing in them that affects my preferred configuration.
